subject.title: Feature: Distinguish webchat client types (Mac app vs browser)

question: Should agent-visible WebChat client type be exposed as Gateway connect metadata, as explicitly untrusted diagnostic metadata, or not exposed to agents yet?
rationale: Agents could use the field for native-only behavior, deep links, diagnostics, or privileged UX, so automation should not choose the trust semantics or prompt/API carrier.

options.title: Expose Trust-Labeled Gateway Metadata
options.body: Propagate validated connect.client identity into a narrow runtime metadata field and document exactly what agents may trust versus treat as diagnostic.

options.title: Expose Only Untrusted Diagnostics
options.body: Surface a clearly labeled untrusted hint for debugging while forbidding agents from treating it as a capability or permission signal.

options.title: Defer Agent Exposure
options.body: Keep client identity limited to Gateway diagnostics until maintainers design a stronger client-attestation and capability contract.

recommendation.title: Expose Trust-Labeled Gateway Metadata
recommendation.body: Propagate validated connect.client identity into a narrow runtime metadata field and document exactly what agents may trust versus treat as diagnostic.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses Gateway protocol, chat runtime context, and client trust semantics where steipete has the strongest current history signal.
